docs.title: EdgeSync Overview
docs.text: edgesync is a freestanding ANSI C11 static-memory microkernel and Python verification toolkit for wearable clock synchronization and fractional-delay resampling.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
1. Power-of-Two Static Ring Buffer: Embedded inside es_kernel_t (8,424 bytes FP64; 4,344 bytes FP32) with branch-free bitmask indexing and zero heap allocation (nm -u edgesync.o has zero undefined symbols).
  2. Origin-Centered Redescending Huber-RLS Clock Estimator: Tracks affine crystal frequency drift $\alpha$ and startup offset $\theta_0$ in $O(1)$ time per beacon while rejecting asymmetric BLE packet congestion bursts without covariance wind-up via effective forgetting $\lambda_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1 - w(1 - \lambda)$.
  3. Branch-Free 4-Tap Lagrange Cubic Farrow Resampler: Evaluates degree-3 Horner polynomials with exact $\frac{3}{128} h^4 |x^{(4)}|_\infty$ error bounds and deterministic gap fallback under BLE packet drops.

docs.title: C11 Freestanding Microkernel (csrc/edgesync.h)
docs.text:
• es_sizeof_kernel() / es_sizeof_kernel_f32(): Exact compile-time SRAM sizes.
  • es_default_config(double fs_in): Validated BLE wearable default parameters.
  • es_init(es_kernel_t *k, const es_config_t *cfg): Static zero-heap init.
  • es_update_sync(es_kernel_t *k, double t_loc, double t_ref): $O(1)$ Huber-RLS update.
  • es_push_sample(es_kernel_t *k, double t_loc, double x): $O(1)$ ring write.
  • es_farrow_cubic_4tap(xm1, x0, x1, x2, mu): Branch-free 4-tap Horner Farrow kernel.
  • es_resample_at(es_kernel_t *k, double t_ref, double *out_x): Streaming resample (cursor fast path, bounded binary search).
  • es_f32_*: Single-precision storage counterparts (4,344 bytes static SRAM; float32 timestamps relative to two double epoch bases).

docs.title: 1. Compile and Audit the Freestanding C11 Microkernel
docs.text:
make all
make audit
make bench

The make audit target prints exact .text, .data, and .bss sizes via size and confirms zero undefined external symbols via nm -u.

docs.title: 2. Streaming Wearable Synchronization in Python
docs.text:
from edgesync import (
    EdgeSyncConfig,
    EdgeSyncKernel,
    simulate_asynchronous_ble_stream,
    synthetic_ppg,
)

fs = 64.0
ppg = synthetic_ppg(duration_s=60.0, fs_hz=fs, seed=1)
sim = simulate_asynchronous_ble_stream(
    ppg,
    fs_hz=fs,
    drift_ppm=150.0,
    offset_s=1.25,
    outlier_rate=0.10,
    seed=1,
)

kernel = EdgeSyncKernel(EdgeSyncConfig(fs_in=fs))
for t_loc, x in zip(sim["t_loc"][:100], sim["x_loc"][:100]):
    kernel.push_sample(float(t_loc), float(x))

docs.title: Using the WESAD excerpts
docs.text:
The paper's benchmarks use excerpts of the WESAD dataset (Schmidt et al., ICMI 2018). WESAD is licensed for scientific, non-commercial use only, so it is not distributed with edgesync. After obtaining WESAD from its official page and preparing the two excerpt files (wesad_s10_slice.npz, wesad_5subj_events.json), point edgesync at their directory:

export EDGESYNC_WESAD_DIR=/path/to/wesad_excerpts
edgesync demo --wesad-dir "$EDGESYNC_WESAD_DIR"

from edgesync import load_wesad_s10_slice

wesad = load_wesad_s10_slice()          # or load_wesad_s10_slice("/path/to/dir")
bvp, fs = wesad["bvp_64hz"], wesad["fs_bvp_hz"]

docs.text:
from edgesync import verify_c11_python_parity, audit_zero_heap_symbols

print(audit_zero_heap_symbols())
print(verify_c11_python_parity())
